title: Plan AD: AI Children's Picture Book
summary: Storyline → page-by-page script → illustrations → layout → print / digital
scenario: For parents and creators making an original children's picture book — from a one-line idea to a printable or publishable book.

steps.title: Storyline
steps.detail: Expand a one-line idea into a full storyline — protagonist, conflict, turning point, resolution — and check the pacing against a three-act structure. Give the model a list of interests for a 3-6 year old so the story lands in daily life.
steps.tips: Generate three protagonist options and only develop the one that moves you.

steps.title: Page-by-page script
steps.detail: Break the story into 16-24 pages, each with one line of narration plus a visual description (characters, setting, mood, shot). Keep each page's information load even so the art has room to breathe.
steps.tips: Lock the protagonist's look (hair color, outfit) in the descriptions so every later illustration stays consistent.

steps.title: Illustration generation
steps.detail: Generate the art page by page, anchoring the protagonist with a character reference in Midjourney before each page. Save the description of your favorite first image as a template and change only scene and action per page, so the style never drifts.
steps.tips: Use --cref or feed back the previous finished image via image-to-image for the most stable character.

steps.title: Layout
steps.detail: Drag illustrations and text into a canvas, standardize fonts and sizes, and add page numbers, cover and back cover. Use Magic Studio's copy and background features to finish details, then export PDF for print or digital release.
steps.tips: Build one sample page to confirm font size and bleed before batch-laying the rest, so you never redo a whole book.

steps.title: Print / digital
steps.detail: Export a 300dpi PDF for print and check that text isn't clipped or crossing the gutter. Upload to Kindle or a print-on-demand service, or send a preview link to friends for a test read.
steps.tips: Print one or two test pages first to check color and trimming before the full run.

pitfalls.title: Inconsistent characters
pitfalls.detail: Generating the protagonist randomly per page creates a shapeshifter; anchor a fixed character reference first, then vary per page.

pitfalls.title: Text overlapping art / crossing the gutter
pitfalls.detail: Children's books use big type; keep generous margins and never run text across the spine.

pitfalls.title: Generating all pages at once
pitfalls.detail: Test two or three images to lock the style before batching, or the art style will drift out of control.

pitfalls.title: Ignoring licensing
pitfalls.detail: Before publishing on a commercial platform, confirm the commercial-use terms of your model and assets.
